claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only, making multi-cloud nearly impossible.
AWS CDK supports defining infrastructure only in TypeScript and Python.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because CDK is slowed by CloudFormation.
AWS CDK secrets management supports only AWS Secrets Manager.
AWS CDK uses a CloudFormation state file while Pulumi uses Pulumi-managed state.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C#.
SST's Ion is the code name for a new deployment engine; once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and has a free tier.
A Founding Engineer at SST said Pulumi's deployment feels like a natural extension of writing code and can handle things traditional IaC tools can't.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS has an AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the engine ships inside the SST CLI, with state kept in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
Through 2023 SST was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; the team began the Ion rewrite in late 2023, and Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST's 'Moving away from CDK' post says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'

SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, plus a Pulumiverse Vercel provider (@pulumi/aws, cloudflare, command, docker-build, random, tls, @pulumiverse/vercel).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider README describes taking 'a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`'.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) weekly downloads for September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent that now has more GitHub stars than SST.
opencode's growth hasn't changed SST's release cadence or its dependency on the Pulumi engine.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst, formerly sst/sst.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components exist for cross-team visibility, central guardrails, and sharing infrastructure patterns.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
